# Duet Studio

> A browser music studio where a human and an AI agent produce a track together. The whole song — tempo, swing, tracks, drum hits, notes, mixer and transport — is exposed as WebMCP tools on `document.modelContext`, so an agent in the page can read and edit the music alongside the person using it.

Duet Studio is a step sequencer and piano roll that runs entirely in the browser: no account, and the song lives in the tab unless the human makes a share link. Open it in a WebMCP-capable browser (ChatGPT's built-in browser, or Chrome with the WebMCP flag) and the agent gets ears and hands for the song instead of having to click a 32 × 12 grid of tiny cells.

Every edit is attributed to whoever made it (amber = human, violet = agent), a session log lists each tool call with one-click revert, and undo/redo is shared between both parties.

## Tools the agent can call

Read tools (all carry `readOnlyHint`):

- `get_song` — the song as a compact text grid (`|X...x...X...x...|`, one line per track), plus transport state and the human's current selection; long note lists are shortened to stay inside the output budget, and `track` reads one track in full
- `get_recent_changes` — human song edits since the agent's previous song observation
- `list_instruments` — instrument ids, character and recommended pitch ranges
- `get_scale_notes` — the notes of a scale within a range

Write tools:

- `set_tempo` — BPM and swing
- `set_playback` — start/stop the loop (only after the human has clicked once, per browser autoplay rules)
- `set_song_meta` — title, key, scale, bar count
- `add_track`, `remove_track`, `update_track` — tracks and mixer (volume, mute, solo, rename)
- `set_drum_pattern` — replace a drum pattern from text or a `{ hits, steps, rotate }` Euclidean rhythm
- `set_notes` — write melodic notes, replacing or merging
- `set_chords` — turn a scale-relative Roman-numeral progression into voiced chords
- `humanize` — velocity variation on one or all tracks
- `undo`, `redo` — the shared history
- `clear_song` — destructive, so it opens an approve/decline dialog and only proceeds if the human approves
- `edit_selection` — registered only while the human has a selection, so "make *these* steps a fill" is exact

## Pages

- [Studio](https://duetstudio.mehmetcan.me/): the app itself is a single page at `/`; `/?s=<id>` opens a shared song
- [README](https://github.com/mehmetcanbozkus/duet-studio/blob/main/README.md): what it is, why WebMCP fits, and how it is built
- [Source](https://github.com/mehmetcanbozkus/duet-studio): full source, MIT licensed

## Optional

- [WebMCP specification](https://webmachinelearning.github.io/webmcp/): the draft this app implements
